cuisine: Soba (hand-cut buckwheat noodles), traditional Japanese
hours_raw: Location unconfirmed for the Tokyo/Marunouchi pin — could not verify a soba shop named "蕎麦 さとう" in Chuo-ku or Marunouchi. The only soba shop with this exact name and an official site (sobasato.com) is in Mobara, Chiba (lunch 11:30–15:00 LO14:30 / dinner 17:30–20:00 LO19:30, closed Sundays), which is NOT this Tokyo entry. Confirm hours on arrival.
gf_detail: Treat as UNSAFE for a strict celiac unless verified in person. This is a traditional soba shop, and traditional soba is a high-gluten-risk cuisine in three independent ways: (1) Noodles — most Japanese soba is nihachi (二八, 80% buckwheat / 20% wheat) and is NOT gluten-free. Even where a shop offers juwari (十割, "100% buckwheat"), noodles are typically cut on a shared board dusted with wheat flour (uchiko) and boiled in the SAME pot of water used for wheat-containing soba/udon, so cross-contamination is routine. (2) Tsuyu/dipping sauce — standard soba tsuyu is made with regular soy sauce (shoyu), which contains wheat, so even a "gluten-free" noodle is served with a wheat sauce unless wheat-free tamari is specifically arranged. (3) Sides — tempura (ten-seiro, kakiage) uses wheat batter and is often fried in oil shared with the noodle kitchen. For reference, the same-named shop in Chiba lists its house "nami" soba at ~70% buckwheat (≈30% wheat) and its premium "ginbiraki" at 80–100% buckwheat with a nihachi new-soba in winter — i.e. its cheapest soba is decidedly not GF. A celiac should not rely on this entry; ask directly whether they cut a dedicated juwari with no wheat uchiko, boil it in fresh water, and can serve tamari-based tsuyu. Absent all three, answer is no.
vegan_detail: Not vegan by default. Traditional soba tsuyu (the hot broth and the cold dipping sauce) is built on katsuo dashi — dried bonito (fish) flakes, often plus mirin — so both hot kake-soba and cold zaru/mori-soba dipping sauce contain hidden fish. Kaiseki/set courses at such shops also commonly include egg (tamagoyaki, dashimaki), fish, and tempura seafood. Plain soba noodles with no sauce may be orderable, and some shops can make a kombu/shiitake (kelp/mushroom) dashi on request, but this must be confirmed — do not assume. Flag bonito dashi explicitly.

gf_cross_contamination: Wheat flour (uchiko) used to dust the cutting board and prevent noodles sticking
Noodles boiled in shared water also used for wheat-containing soba/udon
Tsuyu made with wheat-containing soy sauce
Tempura sides use wheat batter, often in shared fryer oil
soy_sauce_wheat: Standard soba tsuyu uses regular shoyu, which contains wheat; wheat-free tamari not confirmed available
vegan_cross_contact: Bonito (katsuo) dashi is the base of essentially all soba tsuyu — hot and cold
Sets may include egg and seafood tempura

cultural_comfort.note: Unverified location; for traditional independent soba shops in central Tokyo, assume little to no English and no printed allergen chart. A foreign celiac/vegan should bring a Japanese allergy card (esp. wheat 小麦 and bonito/fish かつお・魚) and confirm noodle composition, boiling water, and tsuyu ingredients directly.

chef_bio.background: No chef or owner could be verified for a Tokyo/Marunouchi shop named 蕎麦 さとう; the pin appears to be an unconfirmed placeholder. (A separate, similarly named 蕎麦さとう exists in Mobara, Chiba, but is a different establishment and its chef was not documented on the pages reviewed.)
chef_bio.specialty: Hand-cut soba (if the shop is confirmed to exist)

cuisine: グルテンフリー フレンチ/イタリアン ビストロ（国産素材・小麦不使用）
hours_raw: Lunch (Mon–Sat) 11:30–14:00 / Dinner Mon–Thu & Sat 17:00–22:00, Fri 17:00–23:00. Closed Sundays. Irregular holidays announced on Instagram (@lei_akihabara).
gf_detail: This is a genuinely wheat-free establishment, not a place that merely offers a few GF items. The restaurant's own name and concept is 「小麦を使わない国産ビストロ」— "a domestic bistro that does not use wheat." A gluten-free blogger who visited reports the chef himself has a wheat allergy ("シェフが小麦アレルギーとのことで相談もできて安心"), so no wheat flour is used anywhere: bread and quiche/pastry are made with rice flour (米粉), and even the signature spice curry is 小麦粉不使用 (no wheat-flour roux), thickened instead with house bouillon and long-cooked whole onions. Because there is no wheat in the kitchen, the usual Japanese cross-contamination traps (tempura batter, shared fryer with breaded items, flour dusting) do not apply here. The one thing NOT independently confirmed on any source page is the soy sauce / seasoning base: ordinary Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, and while a fully wheat-free bistro almost certainly uses a wheat-free tamari, a celiac should still confirm the soy sauce and any sauce/curry base directly on-site. Overall this is one of the safest-looking GF options in the Akihabara area for a celiac, precisely because the whole kitchen is built around avoiding wheat.
vegan_detail: Vegan is not the focus — the menu centers on domestic meat and animal products: Miyagi (Oshika Peninsula) venison cooked sous-vide with beet sauce, mochi-pork ("もち豚") smoked/curry dishes, spinach quiche and chocolate terrine (egg/dairy), and a house bouillon that is very likely animal-based. There are plant-forward items (grilled seasonal vegetables, rice-flour bread), so a vegetarian or flexible diner can eat, but a strict vegan must confirm the dashi/bouillon and ask for meat- and dairy-free versions. No explicitly labelled vegan set was found. Note the GF strength here does NOT extend to vegan — treat those as separate questions on-site.

cultural_comfort.note: Small 15-seat basement bistro; service and menu are in Japanese. An English Tabelog booking page exists, but expect a Japanese-first experience. The upside for a foreign celiac: because the chef reportedly has a wheat allergy himself, allergen consultation is taken seriously — bring your allergy card and confirm soy sauce/dashi. Reservation recommended.

chef_bio.background: The chef is described as being from the Tohoku region and, per a gluten-free blogger, has a wheat allergy himself — which is the origin of the entirely wheat-free concept. The kanda-curry.com curry-grandprix page separately refers to a manager 「店長コバヤシさん」(Mr. Kobayashi), who may or may not be the chef; the chef's full name was not confirmed on any source, so it is left blank rather than guessed.
chef_bio.philosophy: 小麦を使わない (never use wheat) and 国産 (domestic-sourced): body-friendly cooking built on Japanese ingredients, domestic natural wine, and Tohoku produce (Miyagi venison, seasonal vegetables), using rice flour in place of wheat throughout.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-flour bistro cooking — house rice-flour bread baked daily, wheat-flour-free spice curry (house bouillon, cardamom/cinnamon, whole domestic onions), Miyagi Oshika-Peninsula venison, and a cocoa-based gluten-free chocolate terrine, paired with domestic (Tohoku) wines.

The bistro leans on Tohoku ingredients and domestic natural wine, including sous-vide Miyagi (Oshika Peninsula) venison with a beet sauce.

cuisine: Gluten-free rice-flour pancakes & tea cafe (French-influenced)
hours_raw: 10:30–20:00 (L.O. 19:00), 年中無休 (open year-round; located inside Nihonbashi Takashimaya S.C. 新館 3F, so may follow department-store closures)

hours.notes: L.O. 19:00; 年中無休 (open year-round per official site; may follow Takashimaya S.C. closures)

gf_detail: The signature "VAVAパンケーキ" batter is made with 100% domestic rice flour and, per the official site and menu, uses NO wheat flour (「小麦粉を一切使わない」); it is sweetened with beet sugar (てん菜糖). There is also a gluten-free spaghetti (グルテンフリースパゲッティ, 国産米粉100%: 天使の海老 / アラビアータ). So real, deliberate GF items exist. BUT this is NOT a dedicated gluten-free kitchen: the same menu openly serves wheat-based dishes — モンティクリスト (French toast on bread), 天使の海老バーガー (wheat buns), 天然酵母パン・ド・カンパーニュ (bread), and スコーン. Wheat flour and bread are prepared in the same kitchen, so a strict celiac faces genuine cross-contamination risk (shared surfaces, flour dust, shared griddle/utensils); none of the sources confirm separate prep or a dedicated fryer. Published allergen labels on the GF pancakes note egg (卵), dairy (乳), soy (大豆), shrimp (えび) and yam (山芋). Verdict: the rice-flour pancake and the 米粉 spaghetti are legitimate GF orders, but confirm cross-contamination handling in person — the "gluten-free" branding refers to specific items, not a wheat-free premises.
vegan_detail: Not a vegan-friendly menu. It is a dessert/tea cafe: the rice-flour pancakes list egg (卵) and dairy (乳) as allergens, and the flagship drink is Ceylon royal milk tea (dairy). Cream, soft-serve (VAVAソフト) and cheese-forward savory items dominate. A VAVAサラダ / VAVAミニサラダ exists and might be adaptable, but no vegan items are advertised and hidden dairy/egg is pervasive. A vegan should ask item-by-item and not count on a full meal here.

chef_bio.background: cafe VAVA is a concept produced under the '荒谷公彦プロデュース' restaurant group, per the official site's concept page. The savory menu (pasta, Monte Cristo) is described across listing sites as French-chef-crafted, but no individual head chef is publicly named.
chef_bio.philosophy: Balancing 「美味」と「健康」 (deliciousness and health): a gluten-free 100% domestic rice-flour pancake batter for a delicate melt-in-mouth texture, and body-friendly beet sugar (てん菜糖) from domestic sugar beets instead of cane sugar.
chef_bio.specialty: Gluten-free rice-flour 'VAVA pancakes' and premium Ceylon royal milk tea.

anecdotes.text: The official concept page frames the rice-flour pancake as the house signature: 「グルテンフリー国産米粉100％パンケーキ生地」で「とろけるような繊細な新食感」.
The cafe deliberately swaps cane sugar for beet sugar (てん菜糖) as a 'body-friendly' choice across the menu.

gf_cross_contamination: Same kitchen prepares wheat bread (パン・ド・カンパーニュ), scones, burger buns and モンティクリスト French toast alongside the rice-flour pancakes — flour dust and shared surfaces/utensils are a realistic celiac risk
No source confirms separate GF prep area, dedicated griddle, or dedicated fryer
GF status applies to specific menu items (rice-flour pancakes, 米粉 spaghetti), not to a wheat-free premises
vegan_cross_contact: Egg and dairy present throughout (pancake batter, royal milk tea, cream, soft-serve)
staff_allergy_handling: Per-item allergen labels published for the pancakes (卵/乳/大豆/えび/山芋), which shows some allergy awareness, but no stated celiac/cross-contamination protocol

Second GF item available (国産米粉100% spaghetti)

cuisine: Soba (Sarashina-style buckwheat noodles) — casual neighborhood shop
hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:00–21:00; closed Saturday, Sunday & holidays (per Tabelog listing for 更科, Nihonbashi-honcho). NOTE: hours belong to the best-matched shop, not confirmed at the exact pin.
gf_detail: Not safe for a celiac. 更科そば (sarashina) noodles are milled from the refined white inner endosperm core of the buckwheat groat (更科粉／一番粉, confirmed on JA Wikipedia). That pure starch binds poorly, so sarashina soba is bound with a HIGH proportion of wheat flour (小麦粉) as tsunagi — typically MORE wheat than ordinary 二八 soba — meaning the noodles themselves contain significant gluten. There is no juwari/GF noodle here, and even juwari would be 'ask' at best. The dipping tsuyu/broth is made with standard wheat-fermented soy sauce (醤油). The visible menu (Tabelog) is wheat-heavy throughout: tempura soba (天ぷら — wheat batter), curry seiro / curry soba (curry roux normally contains wheat flour), tanuki soba (tenkasu = fried wheat), and katsudon sets (panko-breaded pork). No dedicated GF kitchen, no dedicated fryer, and no allergen program was found. A celiac should not eat here.
vegan_detail: Hidden fish is pervasive. The cold mori/zaru soba noodles are flour-and-water (no egg), but the standard tsuyu is a bonito/katsuobushi (fish) dashi and hot broths (kake soba) use bonito–kombu dashi, so nearly every served dish carries fish stock. Tempura and tanuki (tenkasu) items share frying oil with animal-based fries. No vegan menu, no vegan dashi, and no plant-based labeling were found. At most a strict vegan could eat plain cold soba noodles while declining the tsuyu and bringing/confirming a fish-free dipping sauce — and would still need to verify the noodles themselves and any garnish. Confirm every broth/sauce is dashi-free before ordering.

gf_cross_contamination: Sarashina soba noodles are bound with wheat flour (tsunagi) — high gluten content, not a GF noodle
Tempura is battered and fried in wheat; almost certainly a single shared fryer
Curry seiro / curry soba typically use a wheat-flour curry roux
Katsudon and rice sets use panko (wheat) breading
Flour dusting on noodle prep surfaces cross-contaminates
soy_sauce_wheat: Soba tsuyu (dipping sauce) and hot broths are made with standard wheat-fermented soy sauce (醤油)
staff_allergy_handling: No documented allergen program or gluten-free accommodation found
Small cash-only local shop; limited English — allergy communication would be difficult
vegan_cross_contact: Tsuyu and kake broths use bonito (fish) dashi
Shared frying oil for tempura and tenkasu (tanuki)
positives: Cold mori/zaru soba noodles are egg-free (flour + water)

chef_bio.specialty: Sarashina-style (white refined-core) soba, plus curry seiro, tempura and katsudon set meals

cuisine: 薬膳カレー (medicinal/herbal spice curry) — "sarasara" thin spicy Delhi/Bombay-lineage curry, flour-free
hours_raw: お茶の水本店: Lunch 11:00–15:30 (L.O. 15:00); dinner (18:00–22:00) currently suspended — lunch only. Closed Mondays & Wednesdays (open on public holidays, closed the following day instead); also summer break and year-end holidays. NOTE: the 神保町 (Jimbocho) branch has permanently closed; this is the main Ochanomizu store ~5 min walk from Jimbocho Sta. A5 exit.
gf_detail: The restaurant explicitly brands its signature curries as "小麦粉を使わないグルテンフリーカリー" (gluten-free curry made WITHOUT wheat flour) on its official site. The roux is built from a homemade aromatic vegetable broth and 20+ medicinal spices rather than the wheat-flour roux used in typical Japanese curry, which removes the usual gluten source — a genuine, unusually strong GF positive for a Tokyo curry shop. CAVEATS for a celiac: (1) it is NOT a dedicated gluten-free kitchen — no dedicated fryer/equipment claim, so cross-contact cannot be assumed; (2) the "べっぴん牛スジカリー" braises beef tendon in red wine and dishes are simmered in wine — wine is generally GF but confirm no flour is added; (3) confirm no wheat in any garnish/pickle or side, and that the base is plated over rice only (no naan); (4) no English is spoken, so verifying cross-contamination on site may be difficult — bring a Japanese allergy card. Not a soba shop, so juwari-soba wheat risk is not applicable here.
vegan_detail: All four signature curries contain animal protein: domestic chicken (赤の薬膳カリー red herbal curry and 黒のカシミールカリー black Kashmir curry), soft-shell shrimp + coriander (shrimp curry), or beef tendon braised in red wine (牛スジカリー). No vegan or vegetarian menu item is advertised. The curry base is described as a homemade aromatic vegetable soup with 20+ spices and eight vegetables simmered in wine, and no bonito/katsuo dashi is mentioned — so the base itself may be plant-derived, but this is not confirmed and the finished dishes all include meat/seafood. A vegan diner should ASK whether a vegetable-only (chicken-omitted) version is possible; do not assume.

cultural_comfort.note: Small counter-style lunch curry shop, Japanese-only menu and signage; no English capability noted. Cash only. Ordering is simple in practice (choose a curry and a spice level 1–6), and staff are described as courteous and gentle, but expect to communicate in Japanese — bring a written allergy/GF card if celiac.

chef_bio.background: べっぴん舎 carries the classic Tokyo Indian-curry lineage: it descends from 柏『カレーハウスボンベイ』(Curry House Bombay, Kashiwa), which itself trained under 上野『デリー』(Delhi, Ueno) — Japan's pioneering Indian curry restaurant. The owner-chef also came from a wine-bistro background, which is reflected in the wine-braised preparations and the beer/wine pairings offered.
chef_bio.philosophy: A deliberately flour-free, gluten-free 'yakuzen' (medicinal) spice curry: rather than a wheat-flour roux, the curry is built from a self-made aromatic vegetable broth and 20+ proprietary medicinal spices for a clean, refreshing 'sarasara' (thin) finish said to aid metabolism. Framed as distinct from soup curry.
chef_bio.specialty: 赤のべっぴん薬膳カリー (Red Beppin Herbal Curry) — cardamom, ginger and plenty of onion with domestic chicken and seasonal vegetables (eggplant, carrot, lotus root, broccoli), spice levels 1–6.

anecdotes.text: Four-time recipient of the Kanda Curry Grand Prix Meister Award, a Tabelog Top-100 (Hyakumeiten) regular, and selected as a Bib Gourmand in the Michelin Guide Tokyo (2021).
The shop describes its curry as '小麦粉を使わないグルテンフリーカリー' — a gluten-free curry made without wheat flour, using homemade aromatic vegetable broth, eight wine-simmered vegetables and 20+ medicinal spices.
Its style is explicitly the thin, spicy 'sarasara' curry inherited from the Delhi (Ueno) → Bombay (Kashiwa) lineage rather than a thick Japanese roux curry.

Dishes are simmered/braised in wine (esp. beef-tendon curry in red wine); wine is generally GF but confirm no flour is added
Confirm no wheat in any garnish, pickle, or side and that curry is served over rice only
soy_sauce_wheat: No soy-sauce-based roux is used — the curry is spice/vegetable-broth based rather than a Japanese wheat-flour+shoyu style; no soy sauce wheat risk was documented, but confirm on site
vegan_cross_contact: Shared pans used for chicken, shrimp and beef curries — a vegetable-only request would share equipment
staff_allergy_handling: No documented allergy-handling protocol; Japanese-only, so bring a written GF/celiac card

No bonito dashi mentioned in the base
Michelin Bib Gourmand (Tokyo 2021) and 4x Kanda Curry Grand Prix Meister — well-regarded, consistent kitchen

cuisine: グルテンフリー米粉バウムクーヘン専門店 (gluten-free rice-flour baumkuchen / Western confectionery, takeaway)
hours_raw: 10:00–19:00; closed Saturday & Sunday (定休日 土曜・日曜)
gf_detail: Specialty shop where the ENTIRE product line is gluten-free. Baumkuchen is made from LA VORO's own freshly milled rice flour (自家製生米粉・常陸小田米 / Hitachi-Oda rice) with no wheat flour; two GF varieties — "Eterno" (¥1,080+, whipped-cream, moist) and "Moncone" (¥2,808+, fermented-butter, crisp/chewy) — plus financier-style "Lamet" bakes and one-bite "Cut Baum", all stated gluten-free (ichigaya.keizai.biz; entamemaimai blog). This is a takeaway confectionery, NOT a soba/tempura/teishoku kitchen, so the classic Japanese wheat traps (wheat-based shoyu/tsuyu, tempura batter, shared fryer, flour dusting on a shared surface) do not apply here. Caveat for a strict celiac: I found no explicit "dedicated allergen-free facility" or celiac/gluten certification statement, so cross-contact of add-in ingredients or flavorings is not formally guaranteed — worth confirming at the counter, but the wheat risk is inherently very low for an all-rice-flour operation.
vegan_detail: Not vegan. Baumkuchen is egg- and dairy-based: "Eterno" is made with whipped cream and eggs, "Moncone" with aromatic fermented butter (発酵バター). Products are gluten-free but built on eggs, butter and cream, so there is no vegan option here. Gluten-free ≠ vegan at this shop.

cultural_comfort.note: Tiny takeaway confectionery counter by Iidabashi Station A5 exit — a purchase is a simple point-and-buy of boxed baumkuchen, so language is a low barrier, but assume staff communicate mainly in Japanese. Tabelog has an English page, but the shop itself offers no confirmed English service.

chef_bio.background: Founder/owner and CEO of Opus (オーパス), a Tsukuba-based company, and involved in rice cultivation and sales through Tsukuba Farm. He launched LA VORO's original store in Tsukuba (2019) and opened this Iidabashi second location around 3 April 2024.
chef_bio.philosophy: Pursues 6次産業化 (sixth-industry integration) — carrying his own self-brand rice all the way from production through processing to retail. He chose baumkuchen as the vehicle for that rice and treats it as craft: the shop name LA VORO evokes the Italian sense of 'artwork', and he says he regards each baumkuchen as his creation, made carefully, and wants to engage earnestly with the shop's operation.
chef_bio.specialty: Gluten-free rice-flour baumkuchen made from house-milled fresh rice flour (Hitachi-Oda rice).

anecdotes.text: Ogakubo, a Tsukuba rice grower, wanted to make processed goods from his own self-brand rice and achieve full farm-to-shelf 'sixth-industry integration'; after deliberating on the right product, he settled on baumkuchen made from rice flour.
The name LA VORO means 'artwork' in the Italian sense; Ogakubo says 'we consider the baumkuchen our creation and craft it carefully, and want to earnestly engage with running the store.'

gf_cross_contamination: No explicit dedicated allergen-free facility or celiac/gluten certification statement was found on the official BASE shop or press coverage.

All products are rice-flour based with no wheat flour used, so inherent wheat cross-contact risk is low, but add-in ingredients/flavorings are not formally guaranteed wheat-free — confirm at the counter if extremely sensitive.
vegan_cross_contact: All items contain eggs and dairy (butter/cream); no vegan line, so no cross-contact controls for vegans.
staff_allergy_handling: No documented allergy-handling protocol found; this is a small takeaway confectionery counter.
positives: Entire product range is gluten-free — no wheat flour on the menu at all.
Made with LA VORO's own house-milled fresh rice flour (Hitachi-Oda rice); GF is the core of the brand, not an afterthought.
Takeaway confectionery, so none of the classic Japanese wheat hazards (wheat shoyu/tsuyu, tempura batter, shared fryer) are present.

cuisine: Gluten-free rice-flour bakery (米粉パン) — savory filled breads, curry pan, rice-crust pizza
hours_raw: Mon 11:00–15:00; Thu–Sun 11:00–17:00; closed Tue & Wed. Small bakery — operating days can shift, so confirm the current schedule on Instagram (@yeswehackrice) before going.
gf_detail: Fully dedicated 100% gluten-free bakery — there is NO wheat flour on the premises. Everything is baked from rice flour (specially grown Koshihikari, rice bran included), natural yeast, kibi sugar and rock salt. Findmeglutenfree lists it explicitly as a "Dedicated Gluten-Free Bakery," and a celiac reviewer (celiacchat.ca) reported no cross-contamination concerns and that the owner/staff understand celiac disease. Signature curry pan is baked, not deep-fried, so there is no shared-fryer risk. One of the safest bakery options in Tokyo for a celiac. Caveat: savory items (curry fillings, cheese/mayo/shirasu toppings) — confirm the individual filling if avoiding anything beyond gluten, and tell staff "celiac" so they handle it cleanly.
vegan_detail: Not a vegan-only shop, but it carries genuine vegan items among the gluten-free lineup: a chickpea vegan curry pan (¥360), a big vegan marinara/margherita-style rice-crust pizza, and several plain bread rolls/loaves and an "ichizen no pan" with a meat-free bolognese/stew. Many other items are NOT vegan — cheese curry pan, cheese-stuffed rolls, and a wafu pizza topped with cheese, mayo and shirasu (whitebait). Egg/dairy are used in some breads. No bonito/dashi is central to a bakery, but savory fillings should be confirmed. Ask which loaves of the day are egg- and dairy-free; the vegan curry pan and vegan pizza are the reliable picks.

chef_bio.background: Otsuka Setsuko is widely known in Japan as the "Mother of Rice Flour" (米粉の母), a leading figure in the domestic rice-flour movement who is regularly featured in media. She produced and launched RICE HACK Gluten-free Bakery, which opened on November 12, 2022 in Jingumae, Shibuya, operated through 株式会社ライステラス (Rice Terrace / Onden House).
chef_bio.philosophy: That Japanese rice "can change the world" — her breads are not meant as mere wheat substitutes but as foods delicious enough that people with celiac disease or wheat allergy and people without can enjoy the exact same thing together. She emphasizes rice flour's own nutritional properties (rice bran, whole-grain character) rather than mimicking wheat.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-flour bread and gluten-free baking — the shop's signature is a fully from-scratch baked curry pan (homemade curry filling and rice-flour breadcrumbs, crisped in the oven rather than deep-fried).

anecdotes.text: Produced and opened RICE HACK on Nov 12, 2022 in Jingumae, described as a bakery where the completely gluten-free rice-flour dough uses specially cultivated Koshihikari, kibi sugar, rock salt and natural yeast.
A celiac visitor described the staff and owner as "wonderful" and passionate about rice-flour baking, and was struck that the gluten-free bread was still good untoasted the next day.

gf_cross_contamination: 100% dedicated gluten-free facility — no wheat flour is used or present on the premises (rice flour only)
Findmeglutenfree lists it as a "Dedicated Gluten-Free Bakery"; a celiac reviewer reported no cross-contamination concerns
Signature curry pan is oven-baked, not deep-fried, so there is no shared-fryer wheat risk
soy_sauce_wheat: Bakery context — no soba tsuyu or standard shoyu-dressed dishes; savory fillings (curry) are made in-house within the GF kitchen, but confirm seasoning if you react to trace soy/wheat-derived seasonings
vegan_cross_contact: Shared bakery cases hold dairy (cheese) and egg-containing breads alongside vegan items — fine for gluten but relevant if strictly vegan
staff_allergy_handling: Celiac reviewer reports the owner and staff understand celiac disease and are attentive; staff spoke English
positives: Entire shop is gluten-free, removing the usual Japanese-bakery wheat-everywhere risk
Owner/staff knowledgeable about celiac needs
No deep-frying

cultural_comfort.note: Takeout-only window (no seating at the bakery itself, though the adjacent Onden House / Kouji Cafe can seat you for drinks). Menu carries English translations and a celiac visitor reported English-speaking staff, so a foreign celiac/vegan diner can communicate needs comfortably. Simply say "celiac" and "vegan" and point to the labeled items.

cuisine: イタリアン（オステリア）／グルテンフリー生パスタ
gf_detail: Genuine, real GF item: a weekly-rotating gluten-free FRESH pasta that can be substituted for any pasta dish at dinner for +150 yen (税込). The kitchen advertises it as tasting the same as their normal fresh pasta (「食感は普通の生パスタと変わりませんのでぜひお試しください」). This is a rice-flour / GF fettuccine (one reported special: 鴨と焼き茄子・豆苗の米粉フェットチーネ ¥1,200). CELIAC CAUTION — this is NOT a dedicated GF operation: it is a standard Italian osteria whose main product is house-made WHEAT fresh pasta (「モチモチとした食感…の生パスタ」), so the same kitchen has heavy airborne flour, shared pasta water, shared surfaces and utensils. The GF pasta swap addresses the noodle only — sauces, breaded/fried items, the complimentary bread on lunch sets, and flour-dusted prep are all cross-contamination vectors that were NOT confirmed as controlled. There is no published allergen chart and no stated dedicated pot/fryer. Treat as "GF pasta available" not "safe for a sensitive celiac"; a strict celiac should ask (ideally in Japanese) whether the GF pasta is boiled in separate water and whether the chosen sauce is wheat-free.
vegan_detail: Not a vegan-oriented kitchen. A few plant-forward plates exist — 季節野菜のアヒージョ (seasonal vegetable ahijo, ~¥1,180) and vegetable small plates — but the visible meat-free mains are dairy-heavy (e.g. モッツァレラとバジルのトマトリゾット ¥1,480 contains cheese). Being an Italian osteria, expect butter, cheese, cured pork (guanciale/pancetta), and animal-based brodo in risotto/sauces. No labeled vegan menu and no confirmation that risottos/sauces are made without butter, cheese or meat stock. Vegan diner should specify no cheese/butter/meat/fish and confirm each dish; realistically limited to the vegetable ahijo, plain vegetable sides, and possibly a tomato/olive-oil pasta (GF pasta swap) made to order.

chef_bio.background: 料理は「本場（イタリア）で修業したシェフが創るイタリアン」と店が説明しており、シェフはイタリアで修業した経歴を持つとされる。氏名は公表情報では確認できず。
chef_bio.philosophy: 素材重視。肉は「赤身と脂のバランスを、シェフ自らが吟味し厳選したお肉だけを使用」とし、パスタは自家製の生パスタにこだわる。店のコンセプトは『気軽にワインを愉しむ居酒屋（オステリア）』で、仕事帰りに飲んで食べて疲れを癒やす場を志向。
chef_bio.specialty: 自家製生パスタ、名物リゾット、国産牛サーロインのタリアータ。ディナーではグルテンフリー生パスタへの変更に対応。

anecdotes.text: 肉は赤身と脂のバランスをシェフ自らが吟味・厳選したものだけを使用していると店が明言している。
毎週替わりのグルテンフリー生パスタを用意し、通常の生パスタと食感が変わらないと案内している。

Chef-selected ingredients and house-made pasta suggest attentive, made-to-order cooking that can accommodate a clearly stated request
Substitution is inexpensive (+150 yen) and staff are used to the GF request

cuisine: Gluten-free organic Japanese/Western (GIG-certified GF specialty restaurant)
hours_raw: Morning 7:00–9:30 (L.O. 9:00); Lunch 12:00–16:00 (L.O. 15:00); Dinner 17:00–22:00 (L.O. 20:30). The official site lists this branch as closed Wednesdays (lunch/dinner), though the Gnavi listing states 年中無休 (open year-round) — confirm the closed day before a special trip. Located on the 1F of APA Hotel Ueno Hirokoji, 〒101-0021 東京都千代田区外神田5-3-3.
gf_detail: This is a fully dedicated gluten-free kitchen — arguably the safest celiac option in the neighborhood. It is certified by The Gluten Intolerance Group (GIG), promoted as "Asia's first gluten-free certified restaurant," and the entire menu excludes wheat, barley, and rye (uses rice flour, etc.). Because no wheat is handled on-site, the frying oil and cooking surfaces carry no wheat-batter cross-contamination, and the soy sauce/seasonings are wheat-free consistent with the GIG certification (no juwari-soba trap here). Two honest caveats the operator itself states: (1) some purchased ingredients "may be processed in facilities that also handle wheat," and (2) the kitchen is small, so they cannot guarantee safety for every allergy beyond gluten. For a celiac this is still an excellent choice; the residual risk is supplier-side, not in-house prep.
vegan_detail: Not a fully vegan restaurant — the menu includes chicken dumplings (rice-flour gyoza), Cajun-spice karaage, orange/rice-flour chicken, pancakes and muffins (egg/dairy). But there are real, clearly labeled vegan options, including a dedicated vegan ramen, and the restaurant is listed on the Vegewel vegan directory. It accommodates egg/dairy/nut/soy allergies "where possible." Flag hidden dashi/bonito: several non-vegan ramen (shoyu, miso-butter-corn, rich "yamitsuki") likely use animal or bonito stock, so a vegan should order the explicitly vegan ramen/dishes and confirm the broth is dashi-free rather than assume.

cultural_comfort.note: Foreigner-friendly: the brand runs an English website (glutenfree.co.jp/en) and takes English reservations via TableCheck, and it is a well-known destination for visiting celiac travelers. Staff are used to allergy questions in English; menus/allergen info are available in English.

chef_bio.background: Owner and chef of Gluten Free T's Kitchen. Raised by a skilled home cook, she grew up surrounded by good food and internalized the idea that 'people naturally smile when they eat something delicious,' developing a passion for cooking from childhood. While living in the United States she saw how common gluten-free restaurants were there compared with Japan, where they were almost nonexistent.
chef_bio.philosophy: To 'become a catalyst for smiles for people who need gluten-free food' — proving through daily recipe and product development that gluten-free meals can be both safe and genuinely delicious, so that people with gluten intolerance no longer have to give up on eating well.
chef_bio.specialty: GIG-certified fully gluten-free Japanese/Western dishes built on rice flour: rice-flour gyoza, orange/rice-flour chicken, Cajun karaage, and multiple gluten-free ramen (including a vegan ramen).

anecdotes.text: Iino was inspired to open a gluten-free specialty restaurant after moving to the US and noticing abundant gluten-free options there, while realizing that many people in Japan with gluten intolerance had 'given up on eating delicious food' because of dietary restrictions.
Under her direction the restaurant became what it bills as Asia's first restaurant certified gluten-free by The Gluten Intolerance Group (GIG), excluding wheat, barley and rye across the whole menu.

staff_allergy_handling: Accommodates non-gluten allergies (egg, dairy, nut, soy) 'where possible'

cuisine: Gluten-free multi-cuisine (rice-flour ramen, orange chicken, karaage, tempura, gyoza) — Asia's first GIG-certified fully gluten-free restaurant
hours_raw: Morning 7:00–9:30 / Lunch 12:00–16:00 / Dinner 17:00–22:00 (L.O. ~21:30). Closed Wednesdays for lunch & dinner (morning service still runs Wed 7:00–9:30). Otherwise open year-round.

hours.note: Wednesday lunch & dinner closed; morning service only. Sources: glutenfree.co.jp and Tabelog differ slightly on lunch end time (16:00 vs 15:00) — confirm.

gf_detail: This is one of the safest GF options in Tokyo for a celiac. It is a fully gluten-free establishment — Asia's first restaurant certified by The Gluten Intolerance Group (GIG) — using NO wheat, barley, or rye anywhere on the premises, plus no chemical seasonings. Because the whole kitchen is wheat-free, the structural wheat traps a celiac normally worries about are removed: soy sauce is gluten-free tamari, ramen uses rice-flour noodles (not wheat), and fried items (karaage, tempura, gyoza) are battered/wrapped in rice flour rather than wheat, so the fryer is not shared with wheat batter. Important caveat the restaurant states itself: some ingredients are sourced from facilities that also process wheat, and they warn that "allergies cannot be guaranteed for all meals due to limited cooking space." So while gluten is structurally excluded, a highly sensitive celiac should still flag their sensitivity when ordering. Note this is NOT a soba shop — the juwari-soba wheat-tsuyu concern does not apply here.
vegan_detail: Vegan is accommodated but this is not a vegan restaurant — the core menu is meat-forward (orange chicken, tonkotsu/pork ramen, chicken ramen, karaage). Dedicated vegan items exist (vegan miso ramen is the flagship vegan dish; vegetarian and pescatarian options are also offered), and staff will accommodate vegan and egg/dairy/nut/soy allergies "to the greatest extent possible." Because many dishes are chicken/pork based and use shared prep space, a vegan should confirm each dish individually. Ask specifically whether the vegan ramen broth is fully plant-based (the restaurant markets no chemical seasonings, but confirm no bonito/katsuo dashi or chicken stock in non-vegan broths bleeding over). Best to state "vegan / bīgan, no meat, no fish, no dashi" when ordering.

chef_bio.background: Founder-owner and chef. Grew up in a food-loving household with a skilled home-cook mother, and learned early that 'people naturally smile when they eat something delicious.' Her focus on gluten-free began during time spent in the United States, where she saw abundant, genuinely good gluten-free restaurants — a stark contrast to Japan, where at the time people with gluten intolerance had largely resigned themselves to giving up delicious food. She has researched gluten-free cooking for over 10 years (sparked by a friend's illness) and has done recipe development and consulting on food diversity and allergy accommodation for major companies before opening her own restaurant.
chef_bio.philosophy: To turn dietary restriction into possibility — 食の制限から、可能性を味わうレストラン ('from restriction to tasting possibility'). She wants the restaurant to be 'a catalyst for smiles' for people who need gluten-free diets, proving GF food can be both safe and delicious through continuous recipe and product development.
chef_bio.specialty: Certified fully gluten-free Japanese/Asian comfort food: rice-flour ramen (incl. a vegan miso ramen), orange chicken, rice-flour chicken gyoza, karaage and tempura battered in rice flour, plus a morning menu — all wheat/barley/rye-free.

anecdotes.text: Her restaurant is the first in Asia to earn gluten-free certification from The Gluten Intolerance Group (GIG), the US-based certifier — the credential she pursued specifically so that celiac diners could trust the kitchen rather than take a menu's word for it.
She cites that the Kanto region alone has over 210,000 people with gluten intolerance, many of whom had given up on eating out — the gap she opened the restaurant to close.

The concept grew into a small group: the Ueno-Hirokoji branch (opened March 2024, inside APA Hotel Ueno Hirokoji), the original Roppongi restaurant, and a gluten-free izakaya in Harajuku opening April 2026.

positives: Asia's first restaurant certified gluten-free by The Gluten Intolerance Group (GIG)
Entire kitchen is wheat/barley/rye-free — gluten is excluded at the establishment level, not dish-by-dish
No chemical seasonings
Frying is done in a wheat-free kitchen; batters/wrappers use rice flour, so no shared wheat-batter fryer
Owner-chef has 10+ years of gluten-free R&D and corporate allergy-accommodation consulting
gf_cross_contamination: Restaurant states some ingredients are sourced from facilities that also process wheat
Restaurant explicitly warns allergies 'cannot be guaranteed for all meals due to limited cooking space' — a very sensitive celiac should still flag their sensitivity
soy_sauce_wheat: Uses gluten-free soy sauce/tamari rather than standard wheat-containing shoyu (consistent with a certified wheat-free kitchen); confirm at table if extremely sensitive
vegan_cross_contact: Meat-forward menu (chicken, pork/tonkotsu) shares a small kitchen; vegans should confirm each dish and ask that vegan items not share utensils/broth with meat
staff_allergy_handling: Accommodates vegetarian, vegan, pescatarian, and egg/dairy/nut/soy allergies 'to the greatest extent possible'
Reservations recommended; English online booking via TableCheck

cultural_comfort.note: Foreigner-friendly by design — it serves an international gluten-free/allergy clientele, has an English website and English online reservations via TableCheck, and English-language reviews (Yelp). Spoken-English fluency of on-shift staff isn't guaranteed, but a foreign celiac/vegan diner can expect to be understood and accommodated more easily here than at a typical Tokyo restaurant.

cuisine: グルテンフリーワッフル / chaffle (cheese-and-egg waffle) sandwiches, low-carb sweets & smoothies
hours_raw: Listed hours were 11:00–15:30 (L.O. 14:30), closed Saturdays. IMPORTANT: this Asakusa branch announced permanent closure around December 2022 and Tabelog now flags it as closed/on-hold — treat as CLOSED. Address on record: 東京都台東区雷門2-1-13 (near Kaminarimon gate / Asakusa Station), which differs from the approximate 田原町 pin. The brand (Chaffle's / mincle) continued operating a Sengoku (Bunkyo-ku, 千石4-25-2) location.
gf_detail: Entirely gluten-free concept: the shop is a satellite of グルテンフリー工房mincle (a dedicated gluten-free workshop run by 株式会社M'svision), and its "chaffles" use NO wheat flour and no white sugar — the sweets are naturally wheat-free, so cross-contamination from flour is inherently very low because wheat flour is not used on premises. Caveat for a strict celiac: the savory chaffle sandwiches (e.g. bacon-egg-cheese, honey-mustard) rely on sauces/condiments whose soy-sauce or seasoning base was not confirmed wheat-free in any source I found, so a coeliac should confirm each sauce. Overall a genuinely strong GF operation rather than a token option — but note the Asakusa location appears permanently closed; the Sengoku/千石 branch is the one to verify. Not rated 'dedicated' only because no explicit certified-dedicated-facility statement was located.
vegan_detail: Core product is not vegan: a "chaffle" is by definition a cheese-and-egg waffle, so the signature waffle sandwiches contain egg and dairy. Sources mention "vegetarian options" and specialty smoothies, but vegetarian is not vegan and no confirmed fully plant-based item was found — a vegan should ask specifically and assume the waffles themselves are off-limits. Watch for hidden dairy/egg throughout the menu.

chef_bio.chef_name: Natsumi (product/manufacturing lead) — mincle / 株式会社M'svision, representative 赤荻未加 (Mika Akaogi)
chef_bio.background: Chaffle's is produced by グルテンフリー工房mincle, a gluten-free confectionery workshop operated by 株式会社M'svision (representative director 赤荻未加). Product development and manufacturing are led by Natsumi, described as a former daycare/nursery head nutritionist who worked roughly five years as a lead nutritionist across several nurseries before moving into gluten-free sweets production.
chef_bio.philosophy: Wellness-first, additive-conscious cooking drawing on a nursery-nutritionist background: no wheat flour, no white sugar, and no chemical additives, using higher-quality ingredients so people with wheat sensitivity can eat freely.
chef_bio.specialty: 'Chaffles' — low-carb cheese-and-egg waffles (a keto-origin Western trend) served as sweet and savory sandwiches, plus gluten-free cakes and smoothies.

anecdotes.text: mincle announced Chaffle's as a new gluten-free waffle-sandwich business format, describing the chaffle as a low-carb cheese-and-egg waffle that had become popular among keto dieters in the West a few years earlier, made with no wheat flour or white sugar.
The menu is described as developed by a former daycare nutritionist focusing on high-quality ingredients, with specialty smoothies and vegetarian options alongside the gluten-free waffle sandwiches.

gf_cross_contamination: No wheat flour is used anywhere in the shop's chaffle production, so airborne/shared-flour cross-contamination is inherently low.
Savory sandwich sauces/condiments (e.g. honey-mustard, seasonings) were not confirmed wheat-/soy-sauce-free in any source — a coeliac should confirm each sauce.
soy_sauce_wheat: Savory chaffle sandwiches may use seasonings/soy-based sauces; wheat-content of these was not documented — ask before ordering.
vegan_cross_contact: Egg and cheese are core to every chaffle; shared batter/griddle means egg and dairy are pervasive.
staff_allergy_handling: Brand is a dedicated gluten-free workshop (mincle) founded/led by a former nursery nutritionist, so allergy-awareness is central to the concept.

Run by a dedicated gluten-free specialist brand (mincle) with a professional-nutritionist background.
Explicitly markets no wheat flour, no white sugar, no chemical additives.

cuisine: グルテンフリー米粉スイーツ / rice-flour churros (gluten-free dessert stand)
hours_raw: Mon–Thu 10:00–21:00; Fri 10:00–22:00; Sat/Sun/Holidays 9:00–21:00. Open year-round. Takeout-only stand inside JR Ueno Station (ecute Ueno 3F "Oyatsu Park", inside the ticket gate). Hours follow ecute Ueno; note Tabelog and the official ecute listing agree on this schedule (an older search snippet showing 20:00 closes appears outdated).

hours.notes: Inside JR Ueno Station ticket gate, ecute Ueno 3F. Takeout only. Open year-round.

gf_detail: avan is a dedicated gluten-free specialty brand (グルテンフリー専門店): its products use ZERO wheat flour — only rice flour milled from Yamagata Shonai "Haenuki" rice — and the brand explicitly targets "invisible" wheat hidden in seasonings, marketing itself as "完全小麦不使用" (completely wheat-free). The Ueno store is a takeout churro stand that deep-fries its rice-flour churros in dedicated rice oil (米油); because the whole operation is wheat-free, nothing containing wheat is fried or handled on premises, so there is no wheat-batter or shared-wheat-fryer cross-contamination on site. This is a sweets stand — no soba, no soy-sauce/tsuyu, no tempura. The Shibuya flagship (SANTALE/avan) is independently listed as a "Dedicated Gluten-Free Dessert Shop." Residual caution for a strict celiac: this is a busy station kiosk, so a customer should still confirm no shared tongs/surfaces with any non-GF partner stalls in the "Oyatsu Park" zone — but avan's own product line contains no wheat.
vegan_detail: Not a vegan shop. The base rice-flour churro batter is fried in rice oil and reported (san-tatsu / press coverage) to use no wheat and, for plain versions, no egg or dairy — but the Ueno store's SIGNATURE offering is the "RICH CHURRO" line built around fresh whipped cream (生クリーム), which is dairy. Flavor coatings and add-on gluten-free ice cream may also contain dairy. There is no bonito/dashi concern (it is a dessert stand). A vegan should ASK which specific churro flavors are prepared without cream/dairy and avoid the cream-topped "RICH" items; treat any given item as non-vegan until confirmed.

chef_bio.chef_name: 飯田珠門 (Iida Shumon), founder; wife 飯田弥亜 (Iida Mia) is store manager
chef_bio.background: Iida Shumon founded the avan gluten-free sweets line (café SANTALE in Shibuya; the Ueno stand is 'GLUTEN FREE CAFE avan'). He came to gluten-free through his own health: while watching his diet he cut out wheat and found his physical condition improved markedly, which led him to develop a gluten-free menu. His wife Mia's family runs a rice-flour production business in Yamagata's Shonai region, which became the catalyst for building the products around Shonai 'Haenuki' rice flour.
chef_bio.philosophy: Complete wheat elimination — not just swapping flour but chasing down 'invisible' wheat in seasonings — while making gluten-free sweets that anyone would enjoy for taste alone. The name 'avan' is from French 'avant' (~before): a treat to grab casually 'before' heading somewhere.
chef_bio.specialty: Freshly fried 100% rice-flour churros (米粉チュロ) fried in rice oil; the Ueno store centers on whipped-cream 'RICH CHURRO' variants.

anecdotes.text: Iida says he was originally just watching his diet, cut wheat out, and felt so much better that it pushed him to create gluten-free options: 「もともとダイエットに気を使っていたこともあり、小麦を抜いてみたところ、体のコンディションがとてもよくなりました」
The rice-flour focus traces to his wife's family, who produce rice flour in Yamagata's Shonai region — the shop uses top-grade Shonai 'Haenuki' rice.
The brand markets itself as fully wheat-free, watching even for wheat hidden in seasonings: 「粉の小麦だけでなく、調味料に入っている目に見えない小麦にまで着目し、完全小麦不使用を徹底している」

gf_cross_contamination: No wheat cross-contamination risk from avan's own products: the entire brand is 100% wheat-free, so no wheat batter, wheat flour, soy sauce, or tempura is present.
Churros fried in dedicated rice oil (米油) used only for avan's gluten-free items.

Residual caution: this is a takeout kiosk in ecute Ueno's shared 'Oyatsu Park' sweets zone — a strict celiac should confirm avan uses its own tongs/counter and does not share utensils with adjacent non-GF stalls.
vegan_cross_contact: Fresh dairy whipped cream (生クリーム) is used at the Ueno store on the signature 'RICH CHURRO' line.
Add-on gluten-free ice cream and some flavor coatings may contain dairy.
Cream and plain churros may be handled at the same small counter — cream contact possible.
staff_allergy_handling: Gluten-free-specialty operation; items are clearly presented as gluten-free (celiac bloggers describe treats as clearly marked GF).
Confirm at counter for a strict celiac, and ask which flavors are dairy-free for vegans.
positives: Dedicated gluten-free brand — zero wheat flour, rice flour from Yamagata Shonai 'Haenuki' rice.
Fried in dedicated rice oil, not shared with wheat products.
Brand explicitly avoids hidden wheat in seasonings ('完全小麦不使用').
Well-labeled, celiac-blogger-vetted, inside a major station — easy takeout for a traveler.

cultural_comfort.note: Small takeout churro kiosk inside JR Ueno Station — interaction is minimal (point, pay, go). The avan brand runs a bilingual Japanese/English Instagram (@avan_sweets_) and items are clearly labeled gluten-free, so a foreign celiac can order with little Japanese, though staff English at the stand is not guaranteed.

cuisine: Udon / soba (うどん・そば)

Do NOT assume any dish is safe. A celiac must confirm in person, in Japanese, whether there is a genuinely wheat-free noodle (e.g. certified GF rice/juwari) cooked in unshared water with a wheat-free soy sauce before eating. Until verified on-site, treat as not safe.
vegan_detail: UNVERIFIED — no menu found. At any standard udon/soba shop the broth (tsuyu/dashi) is typically made with katsuobushi (bonito) and/or niboshi, so it is not vegan by default and the fish is hidden in the liquid even for plain noodles. A vegan would need to confirm on-site whether a kombu/shiitake-only (精進/vegan) dashi is available. No plant-based options could be confirmed.

gf_cross_contamination: Unverified establishment; assume worst case. Udon = wheat noodles. Soba (including juwari/10-wari) shares boiling water and flour-dusting surfaces with wheat noodles.
Tsuyu/broth almost certainly uses wheat-containing soy sauce (醤油).
Tempura (if served) uses wheat batter and likely a shared fryer.
soy_sauce_wheat: Standard tsuyu/dipping sauce at udon-soba shops uses wheat-based soy sauce unless explicitly stated otherwise.
vegan_cross_contact: Broth typically contains bonito/fish dashi even for plain noodle bowls.

cultural_comfort.note: Could not verify the restaurant exists online, so no information on English-language accommodation. A small neighborhood udon/soba shop in this area would typically be Japanese-only; a foreign diner should bring a guide or written Japanese allergy card. Verify the place is real and open before routing anyone here.

cuisine: Gluten-free rice-flour bakery (米粉パン)
hours_raw: Mon & Wed–Fri 10:00–18:00; Sat/Sun/holidays 09:00–18:00; closed Tuesdays (平日10:00–18:00、土日祝9:00–18:00、火曜定休)
gf_detail: Fully dedicated, completely gluten-free bakery — the strongest celiac option imaginable in this dataset. The company states production takes place in a "小麦を持ち込まない完全グルテンフリー製造工場" (a completely gluten-free manufacturing plant where wheat is never brought onto the premises), so there is no shared wheat flour and no cross-contamination from a mixed kitchen. Marketing explicitly targets wheat-allergy, celiac (セリアック病), and gluten-intolerance customers. Bread is 100% domestic rice flour (自家ブレンド米粉) with rice oil (こめ油), beet sugar (てんさい糖) and Okinawan salt; no wheat anywhere. Some SKUs are advertised as アレルギー特定原材料等28品目不使用 (free of all 28 designated allergen ingredients). This is a bakery — not a fryer or soba shop — so none of the usual wheat traps apply: no tempura batter, no wheat soy-sauce tsuyu, no flour-dusted surfaces or shared fryer. One caveat: the official site describes pursuing GFCO certification as a goal ("GFCO認証を前提に") but no confirmed third-party GFCO / ppm lab certificate was found, so "completely gluten-free" rests on the maker's own manufacturing statement rather than a published certificate — a cautious celiac may still confirm the specific item/lot. Location note: the dataset's approximate pin (Suidobashi NW ~1.2km) is off; the real store is Bunkyo-ku Kasuga 2-10-19, ~684m from Myogadani Station.
vegan_detail: Not a vegan bakery, but ingredient-driven vegan options exist. The plain flagship loaves — the ビオブレッドS スライス and プティブール — are built from rice flour, rice oil, beet sugar and Okinawan salt (plus tiger nuts / タイガーナッツ in the signature bread), all plant-based with no egg or dairy. However, a large share of the range is clearly non-vegan: reported items include butter, multiple cheeses, sausage/wieners and chocolate chips. There is no vegan labelling or certification and no menu-wide egg/dairy declaration was found, so a strict vegan must confirm the specific product. Because it is a bakery (no dashi/broth cooking), the usual hidden-bonito/dashi risk does not apply — the animal content is straightforward dairy/meat toppings, not concealed stock.

chef_bio.background: Listed as the representative/founder of 株式会社biossa (BIOSSA Inc.), which opened the Kasuga bakery on 18 December 2019. No detailed personal culinary CV was found in the sources fetched.
chef_bio.philosophy: Founded on the conviction that going gluten-free must not mean sacrificing taste or quality — 「グルテンフリーだからといって、味と質を犠牲にしてはならない」 — pursuing healthful, delicious, highly original products made in a wheat-free facility so wheat-allergy and celiac customers can eat safely.
chef_bio.specialty: Completely gluten-free 100% domestic rice-flour bread (米粉パン); signature loaf incorporates tiger nuts (タイガーナッツ); supplies five-star hotels, cafes and restaurants alongside a national mail-order/EC channel.

anecdotes.text: Runs a 'wheat-never-enters' production plant so there is no on-site cross-contamination — the basis of its celiac-safe claim.
Products emphasise clean ingredients — rice oil, beet sugar, Okinawan salt, no margarine or trans fats.

gf_cross_contamination: Completely gluten-free production facility — wheat is never brought onto the premises (小麦を持ち込まない完全グルテンフリー製造工場), so no shared-flour cross-contamination.
No fryer / tempura / wheat soy-sauce operations — it is a rice-flour bakery, eliminating the common Japanese wheat traps.
vegan_cross_contact: Same facility handles dairy (butter, cheese) and meat (sausage) toppings on some products; strict vegans should confirm the specific item, though plain rice-flour loaves are plant-based by ingredient.
staff_allergy_handling: Business is explicitly allergy-oriented — markets to wheat allergy, celiac and gluten intolerance; some SKUs labelled 28-allergen-free.
positives: Dedicated gluten-free facility (no wheat on premises)
100% rice flour, no wheat used anywhere
Explicit celiac (セリアック病) targeting
Some items free of all 28 designated allergens
Bakery format avoids fryer/tsuyu wheat risks

cultural_comfort.note: Small neighborhood bakery in a residential part of Bunkyo; Japanese-language operation. Takeout only, no reservations, cash + cards + QR pay (PayPay/d払い/楽天ペイ/au PAY) accepted. Little English signage expected, but the fully gluten-free premise means a foreign celiac need not negotiate ingredients — anything sold is safe, so a language barrier is low-stakes. English-capable ordering also possible via the online EC shop.

cuisine: オーガニックカフェ・レストラン（グルテンフリー／ヴィーガン対応）
hours_raw: Lunch 11:00–16:00 (L.O. 15:30) / Café 15:30–18:00 / Dinner 18:00–23:00 (Food L.O. 22:00, Drinks L.O. 22:30). Open daily, year-round (年中無休; closed New Year's Day only).

hours.notes: Lunch 11:00-16:00 (LO 15:30), Café 15:30-18:00, Dinner 18:00-23:00 (food LO 22:00, drink LO 22:30). 年中無休 / closed New Year's Day only.

gf_detail: Strong, explicit GF focus — one of Shibuya's better-known GF-friendly organic cafes. Named GF menu items appear across multiple sources: グルテンフリーバーガー / グルテンフリーベジバーガー (GF veggie burger), グルテンフリー唐揚げ (GF karaage / fried chicken), 月替わりのグルテンフリーランチ (monthly-rotating GF lunch), plus GF+vegan sweets (marketed as グルテンフリー・マクロビ・無添加). All lunches come with a 100% pesticide-free salad bar. IMPORTANT for a celiac: no source I found confirms a DEDICATED GF fryer, and this is a full omnivore kitchen frying non-GF items (so a shared fryer is likely unless staff confirm otherwise). No source addresses whether GF-tamari vs wheat-based soy sauce is used in dressings/sauces. Treat GF karaage/burger as celiac-safe only after asking about (1) shared fryer oil and (2) soy-sauce/seasoning ingredients. Not rated 'dedicated' because dedicated-kitchen/fryer separation is unverified.
vegan_detail: Genuine, prominently-marketed vegan offering (ベジタリアン／ヴィーガン menus, vegan sweets made お豆腐やお野菜で作った — from tofu and vegetables, vegan wines) built on 無農薬・無化学肥料 organic vegetables. However this is NOT a vegan-only kitchen — it also serves meat/fish (e.g. karaage is chicken), so cross-contact with animal items is possible on shared equipment. No source states whether soups/sauces use katsuo (bonito) dashi or animal-based stock; hidden dashi is a real risk to confirm. Ask staff to point to the explicitly vegan (ヴィーガン) items and confirm no bonito/dashi in a given dish.

chef_bio.background: BiOcafe opened on Shibuya's Spain-zaka (スペイン坂) as, per its own marketing, one of Japan's first organic cafe-restaurants centered on pesticide-free / chemical-fertilizer-free (無農薬・無化学肥料) vegetables. It is operated under Kumagai Corporation (クマガイコーポレーション株式会社), a restaurant-management company describing itself as a 100+-year, locally-rooted operator. The official site attributes the organic vision to 'オーナーの奥様' (the owner's wife); no named executive chef was found.
chef_bio.philosophy: 『食べて綺麗になるカフェ』 — food as a route to health and beauty: organic, pesticide-free vegetables, plus gluten-free, macrobiotic, additive-free (無添加) and superfood options, explicitly welcoming guests with allergies and dietary restrictions (アレルギーの方や食事制限のある方).
chef_bio.specialty: Pesticide-free all-you-can-eat salad bar with lunch; gluten-free burgers and karaage; tofu/vegetable-based GF+vegan sweets and macrobiotic desserts.

anecdotes.text: Selected for Tabelog's Cafe EAST Top 100 (百名店) in 2025.
Official site attributes the organic concept to the owner's wife (オーナーの奥様) and frames the cafe around eating to become beautiful.

gf_cross_contamination: Full omnivore kitchen frying non-GF items — shared fryer oil is likely for the GF karaage unless staff confirm a separate fryer (unverified in all sources).
No source confirms GF (tamari) vs wheat-based soy sauce in dressings/sauces/seasonings.
Salad-bar buffet format carries general shared-utensil cross-contact risk.
soy_sauce_wheat: Soy sauce / seasoning gluten status not documented — confirm tamari vs wheat shoyu before trusting a dish.
vegan_cross_contact: Meat and fish are on the menu; vegan items may share cooking surfaces/equipment.
Possible katsuo (bonito) dashi in soups/sauces — not documented, confirm per dish.
staff_allergy_handling: Marketing explicitly welcomes guests with allergies and dietary restrictions (アレルギーの方や食事制限のある方), suggesting staff are accustomed to such requests, but no specific handling protocol is published.
positives: Explicit, well-established gluten-free AND vegan program with named menu items.
Organic, pesticide-free (無農薬・無化学肥料) vegetables; additive-free (無添加) focus.
English menu and English-speaking staff available — easy to ask allergy questions.
Tabelog Cafe EAST Top 100 (2025).

cuisine: グルテンフリー・焼き菓子 / gluten-free bakery (unverified)
hours_raw: Not found — no website, Tabelog page, or map listing located to confirm hours.
gf_detail: The dataset name (グルテンフリーベーカリー サンテ, "Gluten-Free Bakery Santé") advertises a fully gluten-free bakery, but I could NOT independently verify this shop exists. Well-documented nearby verified alternatives if this cannot be found: premium SOW (代官山町12-16, 100% vegan+GF sweets) and の・はぎ (Daikanyama, fully GF/vegan ohagi).
vegan_detail: No menu, website, or listing could be located, so vegan status is unknown.
